title: Risk branch
description: One distinct way the mechanism produces the harm. Branches are separate when they take different responses. Carries exactly ONE disposition; owned outside security.

statement.description: The path from mechanism to harm, one sentence.

evidence.description: What rates the likelihood: a prior incident, a precedent, a vendor advisory, present state.

owner.description: The business owner outside the security function whose objective is harmed. They choose the response.

is_governance_gap.description: True for the branch that is a risk with no owner, no tolerance, or no decision — usually underneath the rest.

intermediate_harm.description: Set only when this branch rolls up to a DIFFERENT intermediate harm than its parent — one mechanism can produce different harms on different branches. Omit to inherit the parent's.

top_harm.description: Set only when this branch backs out to a DIFFERENT top-level harm than its parent (e.g. a remote-operative branch under a data-loss parent rolls to regulatory/legal). Omit to inherit the parent's.

disposition.description: EXACTLY ONE. Set by the decision forum, never pre-set by the author. A fallback belongs in the decision record, not as a second disposition here.

decision.description: The decision record that set the disposition.

controls.description: The control(s) that treat this branch. Required at intake for a Mitigate branch; empty = a finding about the catalogue.

csf.description: CSF 2.0 subcategory refs the response lands in. The recorded decision itself is ID.RA-06.

scenarios.description: Illustrations attached to this branch (precedent and/or constructed).

residual.description: After the response. For Accept, equals inherent. Recomputed from control health.
